analysis:
The PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml: head lines 1969-1970 widen the documented provider video ingestion MIME allowlist. The patch adds data:video/x-m4v and data:video/mov, and states that bytes must be an MP4 or QuickTime file. The changed lines are in the T-050 area (inline video plaintext and container handling). The supplied units cover head lines 470-1394, so the changed hunk itself is outside the visible text. Only the patch excerpt shows it, and no code diff is supplied.

I examined the visible threat-model text: TB-007 cache storage, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011 and T-007 to T-041, including T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). It is unchanged context, with no edits to trust-boundary, mitigation or status entries in the supplied ranges. No weakened control, new attack surface or invalidated assumption is evident from the documentation change.

The doc claims that the AVURLAsset forbidAll restriction, decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel and video-count caps, and rejection of http(s) and file URLs remain. It also claims byte-level container verification is added. Those claims depend on provider-swift media ingestion code that was not supplied. The next review pass should check that the matching Swift code (media ingestion and T-050 temp-file handling) actually enforces the widened MIME list with a magic-byte/container check. It should also check that the new x-m4v and mov types add no temp-file plaintext exposure or parser attack surface. That is an unverified contract, not a finding. needs_deeper_review is set because the code backing the doc change is not visible here.
